messages.text: How do changes in AI data centers technology affect the measurement capability required from Oscilloscope?

AI data centers are pushing oscilloscope requirements upward mainly because the interconnects, boards, and power systems are becoming faster, denser, and more noise-sensitive.

### 1. Faster data-center interconnects require much higher bandwidth
AI clusters are moving toward very high-speed electrical interconnects, including **224 Gb/s PAM4 per lane** in cables, connectors, and backplane/mezzanine systems for AI data infrastructure. The knowledge base cites data-center connectivity products supporting **up to 224 Gb/s PAM4** and 25G/lane NRZ to 224G/lane PAM4 channels.  
**Implication for oscilloscopes:** higher analog bandwidth, lower intrinsic noise, better timing accuracy, and PAM4 eye/TDECQ/jitter analysis become essential.  
Citation: raw/Market/OneNote/full-spectrum-data-center-connectivity-brochure.md, section 3.

### 2. PAM4 signaling increases vertical-resolution and noise requirements
Compared with NRZ, PAM4 has four amplitude levels and only one-third the vertical eye opening. That means the oscilloscope must resolve smaller voltage margins while separating noise, jitter, inter-symbol interference, and equalization effects.  
**Required capabilities:** high ENOB, low noise floor, accurate eye/level measurements, PAM4 decoding, jitter decomposition, equalization/de-embedding, and compliance software.

*This specific PAM4 measurement detail is general engineering knowledge, not directly stated in the returned knowledge-base evidence.*

### 3. Optical/electrical interfaces become more important
AI data centers increasingly use high-speed optical engines and transceivers, including **100G/200G/400G solutions**, and the knowledge base highlights silicon photonics and “seamless integration of optical and electrical devices” for high-bandwidth, low-noise, energy-efficient data transmission.  
**Implication for oscilloscopes:** they need to support both electrical and optical validation workflows—electrical TX/RX characterization, optical modulation analysis via optical front ends, clock/data recovery, and correlation between electrical SerDes and optical module behavior.  
Citation: raw/Market/OneNote/Serdes IC IP (2026-8-7)/Serdes IC-IP companies.md, section 174.

### 4. AI server PCBs demand stronger signal-integrity measurement
The knowledge base notes that AI/data-center/cloud systems use **high-end PCBs focused on high-speed and high-frequency applications**.  
**Implication for oscilloscopes:** board-level validation becomes more demanding: differential probing, impedance-related waveform analysis, crosstalk analysis, skew measurement, insertion-loss/de-embedding workflows, and correlation with VNA/S-parameter models.  
Citation: raw/Market/OneNote/AI server PCB (2026-8-12)/AI Server PCB test.md, section 7.

### 5. Dense high-speed differential routing makes crosstalk harder
The evidence specifically calls out high-speed differential-pair routing and crosstalk concerns, recommending ground-signal-ground routing and symmetric routing of high-speed differential pairs.  
**Implication for oscilloscopes:** multi-channel phase alignment, high-performance differential probes, crosstalk measurement, aggressor/victim analysis, and simultaneous observation of multiple lanes become more important.  
Citation: raw/Market/OneNote/snla426.md, section 10.

### 6. PCB material effects create subtle distortion and skew
The knowledge base mentions PCB fiber-weave effects, including rotation of the signaling image plane relative to the underlying fiber weave.  
**Implication for oscilloscopes:** scopes must detect very small timing skew, deterministic jitter, lane-to-lane variation, and waveform distortion caused by PCB materials and routing.  
Citation: raw/Market/OneNote/snla426.md, section 6.

### 7. Power integrity becomes a major oscilloscope use case
AI accelerators and switch ASICs draw very high, fast-changing currents. This creates power-rail ripple, droop, transient response, and PDN noise issues that couple into SerDes links.  
**Required oscilloscope capabilities:** low-noise power-rail probes, high dynamic range, offset capability, GHz-range power integrity measurement, fast transient capture, spectral analysis, and correlation between rail noise and high-speed data errors.

*This power-integrity point is general engineering knowledge; the returned knowledge-base evidence did not directly cite AI data-center power-rail measurements.*

---

## Summary: what changes in oscilloscope capability are required?

| AI data-center technology change | Oscilloscope capability required |
|---|---|
| 112G/224G SerDes, PAM4 links | Very high bandwidth, low jitter, PAM4 eye/jitter analysis |
| Optical engines, silicon photonics | Optical/electrical interface test, CDR, optical front-end support |
| Dense high-speed PCBs | Differential probing, de-embedding, S-parameter correlation |
| More crosstalk between lanes | Multi-channel high-bandwidth capture, aggressor/victim analysis |
| PCB fiber-weave/material effects | Precise skew, deterministic jitter, and distortion measurement |
| High-current AI processors | Low-noise power-integrity measurement and rail-noise correlation |
| More compliance pressure | Automated Ethernet/PCIe/CXL/optical compliance test packages |

In short: AI data centers push oscilloscopes from general waveform viewers toward **high-bandwidth, low-noise, multi-domain validation platforms** for SerDes, optical/electrical interfaces, PCB signal integrity, and power integrity.

AI data-center interconnects are moving to 224 Gb/s PAM4 channels, so oscilloscope measurements must cover much faster serial data rates [4].
AI data centers use 100G/200G/400G optical engines and transceivers, so measurements must address high-bandwidth optical links [1].
Silicon integration of optical and electrical devices drives a need to measure optical/electrical interfaces for bandwidth, noise, and energy efficiency [1].
High-speed and high-frequency PCBs are used in data center, cloud, and AI systems, so board-level signal-integrity measurement becomes more important [2].
High-speed differential-pair routing and crosstalk are identified issues, so oscilloscopes must support differential-signal and crosstalk analysis [7].
PCB fiber-weave effects can affect signaling, so measurements must detect board-induced signal distortion or skew [6].
